newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium fears Burundi sliding to greater violence.
newsitem.headline: Belgium fears Burundi sliding to greater violence.

text.p: Belgium said on Wednesday it feared Burundi was sliding towards greater ethnic violence following confirmation of two massacres in the past month.
"Belgium is very alarmed by the situation and denounces these massacres," Foreign Ministry spokesman Andre Querton told the weekly press briefing.
"We have the feeling there is a major deterioration in the political and security situation in Burundi," he added.
Querton said the Belgian government had received confirmation that about 120 mainly Hutu refugees had been killed by Burundi's Tutsi-led army last weekend.
The latest killings come on top of the reported massacre last month of around 3,000 civilians in the north of the country, he said.

A Burundian army spokesman confirmed on Monday that soldiers shot dead 126 Burundian Hutu refugees who had been expelled from Tanzania and tried to escape from a detention centre in Burundi on Saturday. He said seven soldiers had been arrested.
Querton said European Union foreign ministers would discuss the political situation in the Great Lakes region at a meeting in Brussels on January 20.
